purpose: Make update streams explicitly subscribable and machine-discoverable without confusing feeds with sitemaps.

requirements.title: Publish RSS 2.0
requirements.rule: Sites with public updates, articles, research notes, releases, changelogs, guides, cards, or other subscribable content MUST publish an RSS 2.0 feed. Prefer /feed.xml as the canonical site feed.

requirements.title: Expose HTML autodiscovery
requirements.rule: Relevant HTML entry points MUST advertise the canonical feed with rel=alternate and type=application/rss+xml.

requirements.title: Use canonical absolute URLs
requirements.rule: Channel links, item links and GUIDs MUST resolve to canonical public HTTPS URLs; item identifiers MUST remain stable across rebuilds.

requirements.title: Keep feed dates truthful
requirements.rule: Item publication/update dates MUST come from source content or reviewed release metadata rather than the build wall clock.

requirements.title: Do not declare feeds as sitemaps
requirements.rule: robots.txt Sitemap directives MUST reference sitemap resources, never RSS, Atom or JSON Feed documents.

requirements.title: Preserve locale semantics
requirements.rule: Localized feeds MUST identify the correct language and link only to content appropriate to that feed's locale; a global feed may aggregate locales only when language is explicit per item or otherwise unambiguous.

requirements.title: Validate generated output
requirements.rule: CI MUST verify well-formed XML, required RSS channel/item fields, HTML autodiscovery, canonical HTTPS URLs, deterministic ordering and the absence of feed URLs in robots.txt Sitemap directives.

requirements.title: Keep compatibility formats additive
requirements.rule: Existing Atom or JSON Feed endpoints SHOULD remain available when consumers may depend on them; RSS 2.0 is the baseline subscription surface, not a reason to break compatible feeds.

githubPages.strategy: Generate feed.xml into the published static root during the deterministic build, inject RSS autodiscovery into the shared HTML head/template, and validate the built artifact before deployment.

nextjsAppRouter.strategy: Expose app/feed.xml/route.ts (or an equivalent static-generation path), return application/rss+xml, add RSS autodiscovery in the root layout/head, and derive items from the same canonical content source used by the UI.
